title: Final Statement, Credit Balance Refund and Closing a Memory Care File
content:
Once a Memory Care Residency Agreement residency has been vacated, its account is brought to a final statement and the file is closed.

## Standard

1. **Final statement.** The final statement is issued within 30 days of the vacate date.
2. **Credit balance refund.** A credit balance is refunded to the party who overpaid, or to the estate. A credit balance is a negative amount owed on the memory care account. The refund is issued by check or by one-time ACH, and it books into the account, bringing the credit balance toward zero.
3. **Closing the file.** The file may be closed only when the memory care account balance is 0.00. Closing the file records that the final statement is settled; the residency then moves from vacated to closed.

## Account balance and closing

| Memory care account balance | File may be closed |
|---|---|
| Positive (an amount is owed) | No |
| 0.00 | Yes |
| Negative (a credit balance) | No |

## Illustration (hypothetical figures)

A residency is vacated on 12 April and the final statement shows a credit balance of 410.00, paid in by the resident's family. The final statement is due by 12 May. The 410.00 is refunded to the family as the party who overpaid; once the refund is booked the balance is 0.00 and the file may be closed.

## Basis Q&A

**Who receives a credit balance where the resident has died?** The party who overpaid, or the estate.

**May a file with an unpaid balance of 25.00 be closed?** No; closing requires a balance of exactly 0.00.
